5.0 GENERATORS AND SETTINGS

5.1 The generator file

A generator is one file. It declares what it is and what settings it takes, and has one function that turns settings into geometry. It replaces both V1's Draw registry objects and its scriptInfo scripts.

// generators/parabola.js
/* Parabola: two arms meeting at a corner, nail i of one joined to nail i of the other.
   The classic corner stitch. Settings: the three corner points, the number of steps. */
export const meta = {
  kind: "generator", id: "parabola", version: 2,
  title: "Parabola", tags: ["fundamental"], notes: "The corner stitch."
};
export const params = {
  a:      { type: "point",  default: { x: 100, y: 100 }, handle: true, label: "Arm 1 end" },
  corner: { type: "point",  default: { x: 100, y: 400 }, handle: true },
  b:      { type: "point",  default: { x: 400, y: 400 }, handle: true, label: "Arm 2 end" },
  steps:  { type: "int",    default: 15, min: 2, max: 200 }
  // colour, line width, rotate, scale: the common set (DR-5.6), not declared here
};
export function build(s, k) {            // s: settings, k: the kernel
  const arm1 = k.line({ a: s.a, b: s.corner, n: s.steps });
  const arm2 = k.line({ a: s.corner, b: s.b, n: s.steps });
  return k.geometry({ paths: { arm1, arm2 }, stitches: k.pairwise(arm1, arm2) });
}
export function migrate(old, fromVersion) { /* settings from an older version */ return old; }
DR-5.1build shall be a pure function of its settings and the kernel. It shall not keep state between calls; every call starts fresh (this is what retires V1's shared singletons, P-2).
DR-5.2A generator may export drag(settings, handleName, newPoint) → settings when dragging a handle must change more than that handle (a midpoint handle that moves both ends). Without it, dragging sets the handle's setting.
DR-5.3A generator shall be registered by saving its file; the catalog reads meta and params without running build, and checks the schema once (FR-6.14.4). A failing check shows the generator greyed in its list with the reason.
DR-5.4version is a whole number. A document records the version each layer was made with; on open, migrate brings older settings forward (FR-6.5.6).
DR-5.5Generators are judged by DR-2.5 (readable) above all: a generator should fit on one screen; anything longer is built from kernel parts.

5.2 Settings schema

TypeFieldsControlValue
intdefault, min, max, step 1slider with a number boxwhole number
numberdefault, min, max, stepslider with a number boxnumber
angledefault (degrees), min −360, max 360slider and dialdegrees
colordefault "#rrggbb"colour picker"#rrggbb"
choicedefault, options [..]list, or buttons when 4 or fewerone option
booldefaultcheckboxtrue / false
textdefaulttext boxstring
pointdefault {x, y}, handle true|falsea handle on the canvas, and two number boxes{x, y, z}
pointsdefault [..], handles true|falsehandles; add and removePoint[]
pathRefdefault nullchoose another layer's path{ layer, path }
seeddefault 1number box with a "new seed" buttonwhole number

Optional fields on any type: label, section (groups settings into a tab of the settings panel), showIf (a condition on other settings), help.

DR-5.6The common set, shared by every generator and shown in a standard panel (FR-6.4.9): colour, line width, steps (where meaningful), rotate, scale, opacity. A generator may hide one it does not use (common: { steps: false }).
DR-5.7Every setting's default shall lie inside its limits; the schema check (DR-5.3) enforces it (the V1 registry check found sliders whose settings were not numbers).
DR-5.8A value from a saved file outside its limits shall be kept, shown with a mark, and used: limits guide the slider, they do not refuse a value (D-15).

5.3 Acceptance tests

AT-5.1Saving a new generator file makes it appear in Draw's list within 2 s with no restart (FR-6.9.2); a file with a default outside its limits appears greyed with that reason.
AT-5.2Two Figures layers made from the same generator, one changed, do not affect each other or Draw (P-2).
AT-5.3A document saved with generator version 1, opened after the generator is at version 2, opens with its settings migrated and draws.

6.0 DOCUMENTS, THE POINT TABLE AND WELDS

6.1 Document format

{
  "format": 2,                         // V2's first format; V1 files are format 1 (section 18)
  "createdBy": "sketchpad-v2",
  "title": "Star in a square",
  "units": "mm",                       // "mm" | "in" | "legacy" (V1 pixels)
  "scale": 0.5,                        // mm per document unit; null until set for output
  "nail": { "diameter": 2, "clearance": 3 },
  "nextPoint": 14,                     // point numbers are never reused
  "points": {                          // the point table
    "1": { "x": 100, "y": 100, "z": 0 },                 // a free point
    "2": { "on": "L1", "path": "arm1", "t": 0.5 },       // attached by fraction along a path
    "3": { "on": "L2", "feature": "tip curve #3" }       // attached by feature name
  },
  "layers": [
    { "lid": "L1", "generator": "parabola", "version": 2,
      "settings": { "steps": 15 },                       // only settings that differ from defaults
      "handles": { "a": 1, "corner": 5, "b": 6 },         // handle name to point number
      "transform": { "angle": 0, "tx": 0, "ty": 0 },
      "role": "stitch",                                   // "stitch" | "guide" | "scaffold" | "image"
      "includeInOutput": true, "visible": true, "color": "#1c7ed6", "legacyNumber": 1 }
  ],
  "order": ["L2", "L1"],               // top first; separate from numbering
  "discs": [ { "point": 2 }, { "point": 3 } ],           // which points are nails shown on the canvas
  "output": { "paper": "letter", "margin": 10, "overlap": 10, "labels": true, "colourCycle": false }
}
DR-6.1A document holds no derived values: no drawn geometry, no bounds, no cached positions. Everything shown is evaluated from it (P-3).
DR-6.2A weld is two handles naming one point number (D-3). There is no weld list to keep in step (P-6).
DR-6.3An attached point that can no longer be found (its feature vanished) shall keep its last position, be marked, and be listed by the integrity check (FR-6.18.5); it shall not jump to another feature.
DR-6.4Settings equal to the generator's default are not written, so a changed default reaches old documents unless they set the value.
DR-6.5Files are written with sorted keys and two-space indent, so a diff in git shows only what changed.
[[FIG weld_shared | A weld: two handles naming one point]] [[FIG weld_attach | An attachment: a point found on another layer's path]]

6.2 Evaluation

Evaluating a document gives, for every layer, its geometry, and for every point, its position.

evaluate(document):
  graph = layers as nodes; an edge L1 → L2 when a handle of L2 names a point attached to L1
  if the graph has a cycle: report the layers in it; evaluate the rest; mark the cycle's layers failed
  for each layer in topological order:
    for each handle: position = free point, or the attached point evaluated on its layer (already done)
    settings = defaults + layer.settings + handle positions
    geometry = generator.build(settings, kernel)       // caught here: a failure marks this layer only (FR-6.14.3)
    apply layer.transform to geometry
    record geometry; evaluate attached points that lie on it
  return { geometries, positions, notes, failures }
[[FIG eval_order | Evaluation order follows attachments]]
DR-6.6Evaluation shall be memoised per layer by a key of its inputs (settings, handle positions, transform); a change to one layer re-evaluates it and the layers that depend on it, no others. Target: dragging a handle on a 20-layer figure redraws at 60 frames a second (DR-17.1).
DR-6.7A cycle of attachments shall be refused at the command that would create it, with a message naming the layers; evaluation's cycle handling is the backstop for hand-edited files.

6.3 Acceptance tests

AT-6.1Weld two Parabola corners; drag one: both arms follow in the same frame, with no propagation code (DR-6.2).
AT-6.2Attach a disc to "tip curve #3" of a rose; change the rose's petals from 5 to 7 and back: the disc follows tip #3 throughout and ends where it began.
AT-6.3Save, close, open: the file is byte-identical when saved again with no change (DR-6.5).
AT-6.4A hand-edited file with an attachment cycle opens; the cycle's layers are marked and listed; the rest draw.

7.0 COMMANDS, UNDO AND SESSION

7.1 The command contract

Command = {
  id: "layers.insert",                 // family.name, unique
  label: "Insert object...",
  scope: "tab" | "subtab" | "global",  // section 11 (FR-6.13)
  enabledWhen(ctx) -> boolean,
  whyNot(ctx) -> string,               // shown as the greyed item's tooltip
  run(doc, ctx, args) -> { doc, select? }   // returns a new document; never changes doc
}
DR-7.1Every change to a document is a command (P-7). A command returns a new document; the old one is kept by history unchanged (structural sharing allowed; mutation not).
DR-7.2History is a list of snapshots with a position (A-3). Undo moves back, redo forward; a new command after an undo drops the redo side. The list keeps at least 200 snapshots or 50 MB, whichever is first, dropping the oldest.
DR-7.3A drag is one command, recorded when the pointer is released; intermediate positions are drawn but not recorded. A run of nudges with the arrow keys within 1 s is one command.
DR-7.4A command that throws leaves the document as it was (it never changed it); the error is reported (FR-6.14.3).
DR-7.5"Changed since saved" is the history position differing from the saved position; selection, mode and view are session, not document, and never mark it changed (P-8).
[[FIG undo_stack | Undo: snapshots and a position]]

7.2 Session

Session = {
  tabs: { [tabId]: { open: documentId[], active: documentId, activeLayer: lid,
                     mode: "lines" | "points", showAll: boolean, hidden: lid[],
                     selected: pointNumber | null, zoom: number, pan: {x, y} } },
  activeTab: tabId
}
DR-7.6Tab switching shall be a pure function of session state: the tab shows what its session says. There is no "needs update", "saved" or "restore" decision chain (P-9).
DR-7.7The session shall be written to the journal store as it changes (at most once a second) for crash recovery (FR-6.18.3); on start-up after an unclean exit the owner is offered it back.
[[FIG state_diagrams | Session, document and history kept apart]]

7.3 Acceptance tests

AT-7.1Delete a layer, undo: the layer, its points and its welds are back exactly (document equal to before).
AT-7.2Select a layer and change mode: the figure is not marked changed.
AT-7.3Kill the browser tab mid-edit, reopen: the session is offered back with the unsaved document.
